papers.title: Nanocomposites in 3D Bioprinting for Engineering Conductive and Stimuli‐Responsive Constructs Mimicking Electrically Sensitive Tissue
papers.abstract: Rebuilding damaged or diseased tissue by means of biological additive manufacturing has recently gained lot of attention and shown very promising result. Using biofabrication techniques to mimic and replicate natural tissue as well as cell environment is a very capable way to achieve physiologically relevant conditions. Especially in electrophysiological human tissue like cardiac or neural tissue, proper signal transduction is of paramount importance for appropriate function and cell maturation as well as differentiation. Precisely, these conductive properties are challenging to engineer. However, a lot of outstanding work has been done recently. Therefore, this review focuses on additives, i.e., nanocomposites with intrinsic conductive properties, to the usually nonconductive hydrogels used in 3D‐bioprinting. Recent work on exploiting the properties of these nanocomposites, such as metal nanoparticles (NPs), carbon nanotubes (CNTs), graphene, or MXenes, to alter the nanoenvironment of the manufactured construct toward conductive tissues is presented. An overview of responsiveness to external stimuli, a second intrinsic property of such nanocomposites is provided as well. Furthermore, these materials are critically analyzed concerning their electrophysiology, i.e., cell–scaffold interaction, their biocompatibility as well as their toxicological properties.

llm.relevance_to_user: 此综述仅关注生物打印中的纳米复合导电材料，完全不涉及人工智能或机器学习。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not incorporate any AI/ML into bioprinting workflow stages, lacks experimental validation of AI models, and does not address autonomous decision-making.

summary_zh.motivation: 综述导电纳米复合材料在3D生物打印中的应用，以模拟电敏感组织。
summary_zh.method: 系统回顾金属纳米颗粒、碳纳米管、石墨烯、MXenes等导电填料的研究进展。
summary_zh.result: 总结了导电纳米复合材料在改善细胞-支架相互作用、生物相容性和毒性方面的现状。
summary_zh.validation: 无实验验证，属于文献综述。

summary_en.motivation: To review the use of conductive nanocomposite additives in 3D bioprinting for engineering constructs that mimic electrically sensitive tissues.
summary_en.method: A systematic review of literature on metal nanoparticles, carbon nanotubes, graphene, and MXenes as conductive fillers in hydrogels.
summary_en.result: The review summarizes current progress in cell-scaffold interaction, biocompatibility, and toxicity of these nanocomposites.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation; this is a literature review.
